facts.raw_span: A 63-year-old woman was admitted with insidious upper abdominal pain unrelated to food ingestion and nausea
after an episode of intense acute abdominal pain
She denied hematemesis or melena
untreated dyslipidemia and well-controlled hypertension on methyldopa
She was a smoker of ten cigarettes per day
a palpable, movable mass in the upper abdomen
Laboratory tests, including a complete blood count, were normal without anemia
Abdominal ultrasound showed a large echogenic mass in the gastric antrum compatible with an expansive lesion
a large submucosal bulging mass in the posterior gastric wall with three Forrest III–type ulcerated areas
biopsy attempts failed to sample the submucosal mass, and ulcer biopsies showed only necrotic mucosa
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen demonstrated a well-defined, homogeneous, oval mass arising from the posterior gastric wall, measuring approximately 10×6×11 cm
the lesion had fat-tissue attenuation with central contrast enhancement and trabecular architecture but did not invade the peripheral layers

concepts.why: The presence of a large submucosal bulging mass in the posterior gastric wall with ulcerated areas and the imaging characteristics of the mass, including fat-tissue attenuation and trabecular architecture, are consistent with a GIST.
The fat-tissue attenuation of the mass on CT and its location in the gastric wall could suggest a lipoma, although the presence of ulcerated areas is less typical for this diagnosis.

The submucosal location and the presence of a large bulging mass with ulcerated areas could be consistent with a leiomyoma, although the imaging characteristics described are not as specific for this diagnosis as they are for GIST.

Although less likely given the imaging characteristics, a gastric carcinoma could present as a large submucosal mass with ulcerated areas, but the described fat-tissue attenuation and trabecular architecture are not typical for this diagnosis.
The presence of a large mass with aggressive features like ulceration could suggest a sarcoma, but the specific imaging characteristics mentioned are more suggestive of other diagnoses like GIST.

rationales.F06: A palpable mass is a common finding in various abdominal tumors.
rationales.F09: The presence of a submucosal bulging mass with ulcerated areas is highly suggestive of a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST).
rationales.F11: The large, well-defined, homogeneous mass with fat-tissue attenuation is more characteristic of a lipoma or a GIST.
rationales.F12: The presence of fat-tissue attenuation with central contrast enhancement and trabecular architecture is highly suggestive of a lipoma, while the absence of invasion into peripheral layers argues against a malignant tumor like a GIST or a sarcoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The lesion had fat-tissue attenuation with central contrast enhancement and trabecular architecture, which is consistent with a lipoma, and the lack of invasion of peripheral layers also supports this diagnosis.
